title: improv·artist · topological (Mona Hatoum)
mutation_directive: improv artist: topological via Mona Hatoum

improv_extras.practice: cage, hair, kitchen object as geometry of unease

v1.feedback: The Hatoum cage concept lands well — the parametric torus with Dehn twist and figure-8 pinch is a genuine topological morph, not a rename, and the wire-mesh particle grid reads as a domestic vessel within 2 seconds. The iron-on-parchment palette is restrained and appropriate. Two things to push: the breathing and pinch cycles are slow enough to feel static on first load — consider a slightly more dramatic initial pinch so the topology shift is immediately legible, not discovered after 30 seconds. The form fills the frame adequately but the camera FOV of 34 and distance of 11 leaves moderate negative space — pulling the camera to ~9 or widening FOV to 38 would give the cage more presence and better echo Hatoum's claustrophobic installations.

v2.feedback: The wireframe torus-cage reads clearly as a Hatoum-inflected domestic vessel — the Dehn twist and figure-8 pinch give it genuine topological unease rather than decoration. The oxidized iron palette against parchment is restrained and earned. Two things to push: the cage currently floats centered and symmetrical, which feels too safe — Hatoum's objects unsettle because they sit where furniture would, so grounding it or tilting the axis would add menace. The slow breathing animation is fine but the pinch deformation could be more aggressive at its extremes to make the topology feel like it's trapping something, not just gently morphing.
